scenes.text: You keep all your gold in a wooden chest.
Problem. Someone keeps walking up and stealing it.
So you tie the chest shut with rope. They just cut it.
So you put a giant rock on the lid. They just push it off.
So you add a wooden bolt that slides through a latch. But anyone can just slide it back.
You need a bolt only you can open. So you drop little pins into it, pushed down by springs. Now it is stuck.
Then you carve a key with bumps that lift every pin to exactly the right height. The gaps line up, and the bolt slides free.
Wrong key? The pins stop at the wrong heights. Stuck.
Now the thief can pull all day. Congratulations. You invented the lock and key.
This exact pin idea was used in ancient Egypt, about four thousand years ago. And it is still inside almost every front door today.
